payload.comment:
Preprocessing stage is structurally sound: split sizes match official PathMNIST partitions, integrity hashes are present, augmentation plan (4× via hflip/vflip/rotate90) is appropriate for 28×28 patches, and standardization is well-justified by the channel statistics. However, one factual inconsistency must be corrected before proceeding.

**Primary issue (must fix):** The data_profile.ambiguity_risks text states classes are "inherently ambiguous at 96×96 patch resolution," yet the same artifact's structured field image_shape_hwc is [28, 28, 3]. PathMNIST images are 28×28×3; the 96×96 figure is a hallucinated value. The profiling anomaly already flagged this as an llm_issue, but the erroneous text persists in the data_profile artifact. Any downstream consumer reading the ambiguity_risks narrative will inherit an incorrect spatial-resolution assumption. Correct the reference to 28×28.

**Secondary issues (noted, lower priority):**
1. llm_model_digest is null for qwen3.8 (ollama). All LLM-authored narrative (profiling comment, data_profile ambiguity text, representation_plan rationale) lacks a pinned model fingerprint. This is a reproducibility gap: a different qwen3.8 build could produce different narrative text. Recommend recording the ollama model digest or at minimum the exact model tag/version.
2. The representation_plan rationale attributes "lower mean, higher std" to the "eosin channel." In the channel statistics (means [0.741, 0.533, 0.706], stds [0.124, 0.177, 0.124]), the channel with lower mean and higher std is index 1 (green), not index 0 (red, the typical eosin-associated channel). The mislabeling does not affect the normalization computation but is a factual inaccuracy in the rationale.
3. Test-set domain shift (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) is properly documented in both the dataset_manifest and data_profile. Small per-class test counts (debris n=339, stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592) will yield high-variance per-class metrics; downstream evaluation should report confidence intervals or use macro-averaged metrics. This is correctly flagged and does not block preprocessing.

No deterministic computation errors were found. The structured data fields (class counts, proportions, channel statistics, split sizes, hashes) are internally consistent. The required revision is limited to correcting the 96×96 → 28×28 reference in the data_profile narrative and optionally fixing the channel-label misattribution in the representation_plan rationale.
